Call centre: 18 customers around Veyangoda say data is very slow and calls keep dropping.
Social media post: "heard the Padukka tower is already fixed, the company van came" (unconfirmed).
NMS 06:00 | MAJOR | BER87 Beruwala | AC MAINS FAIL, running on battery bank
NMS 06:00 | MAJOR | PAD85 | rectifier input lost (mains), DC on batteries
NMS 06:00 | CRITICAL | transmission HOM12->PAD85 | fibre/MW path down, no sync

policy.evidence_rule: Authoritative evidence must be consistent; equally authoritative conflicts require confirmation. Recency alone does not verify a fact.
policy.on_crew_loss: Pause affected unfinished work and request operator review; preserve completed repairs.

finding.finding: Verified faults are grid power loss at Beruwala (S01) and Padukka (S09), plus down backhaul link L09 from Homagama (S08) to Padukka (S09). No evidence establishes equipment faults or road closures. No action is deferred: uncertainty alone is not a hold reason, and the catalogue has a generator deployment for S01 and S09 and a link repair for L09; crews C1/C2 have relevant generator skills, while no backhaul-skilled crew is listed, but that is not evidence making an action unsafe or impossible. Approved weights remain unchanged: V09 at Padukka is critical (weight 5), all other services weight 1

findings: The cited authoritative reports support all three extracted facts: Beruwala (S01) has grid power failure; Padukka (S09) has mains/rectifier input loss; and the Homagama-to-Padukka transmission path is down, which the directory identifies as L09. The reports do not establish equipment faults.
The planned generator deployment targets S01. Its route travel is 5 minutes before work starts at minute 5; the 10-minute deployment ends at minute 15, so the arithmetic is consistent.

Unscheduled needs for S09 power recovery and L09 repair are accurately left unmet; no cited evidence establishes those actions as unsafe. The customer complaint, planned future outage notice, and unconfirmed rumour do not establish additional current asset faults.
